Every Petrarchan sonnet is divided into.why: The defining structure of the form, stated in every account of it: 'an octave and a sestet' and its variants occur well over a thousand times in Dolma, and the form's Wikipedia article states it. No real exception: the sestet's rhyme scheme varies (and in English sometimes ends with a rhyming pair), but the division into eight and six lines is what makes a sonnet Petrarchan.

sources.quote: The sonnet is split in two stanzas: the "octave" or "octet" (of 8 lines) and the "sestet" (of 6 lines), for a total of 14 lines.

Keats's 'On First Looking into Chapman's.why: Keats's sonnet is a standard textbook example of the Petrarchan form; its article says so and describes its octave and sestet, the by-name route of w1 and w3. Mentions with the form's name are modest in Dolma, so w2 and w4 (reached through the class) are the likelier worlds for this poem (Decisions 4).

notes: TBox rule edit. Derivability very_unlikely: the octave-sestet division is the form's definition, stated everywhere. No real exceptions: the sestet's rhyme scheme varies, and English Petrarchan sonnets sometimes end the sestet with a rhyming pair (CDDCEE), so no query asks whether the original form 'ends with a couplet'; every query asks the division into sections, which holds for every Petrarchan sonnet. The new rule is the Shakespearean division, a plausible confusion and clearly false. Determinate queries use new sonnets named in the prompt; the background-belief queries use two textbook Petrarchan sonnets, called only 'sonnet' in the prompts (both stay fourteen-line sonnets in every world). Their storage choices are independent, so four worlds. In the by-name worlds the poem keeps its octave and sestet and its membership gives way (README, TBox): neither poem is a founding member of the form (Petrarch's own sonnets are), so no fact outside the chain depends on it. Near query: the form's total of fourteen lines, unchanged by the edit and different from the new answer. Relation divided_into is new and property-free (scratch relations file), adding to the 'none' share (CRITERIA Rule 12). Side fact in every world: the form's rhyme scheme (ABBAABBA plus a varied sestet) is part of the same definition and gives way with the division; it is not a separate firm fact that keeps the octave and sestet. Formal check (FINDINGS C3): the chains now state what makes the two divisions exclude each other (each fixes the closing section's length, and a poem has one closing section), which q1's and q3's 'no' answers and the by-name worlds use.
